title: Conjecture that planar grazes characterize ellipsoids
statement: Let $K,L\subset\mathbb R^n$ be convex bodies with $L\subset\operatorname{int}K$. For a point $x\in\mathbb R^n\setminus L$, let $\Sigma(L,x)$ denote the graze of $L$ from $x$, namely the intersection of the boundary of the support cone of $L$ from $x$ with $\partial L$. Suppose that, for every $x\in\partial K$, $\Sigma(L,x)$ lies in a hyperplane. **Planar-graze characterization conjecture.** Then $L$ is an ellipsoid. The source presents this as an expected extension of known characterizations of ellipsoids by planar shadow boundaries and grazes; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
source_name: Ivan Gonzalez Garcia, Jesus Jeronimo Castro, Diana Janett Verdusco Hernandez and Efren Morales Amaya, “A characterization of the ellipsoid through planar grazes”, arXiv:2207.13294 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.13294

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2022). “This conjecture was first proved by P. W. Aitchison, C. M. Petty, and C. A. Rogers and is known as the False Centre Theorem.”
